title: Precedence and Grouping
definition: Precedence and grouping determine the order in which parts of a compound expression are evaluated.
purpose: Remove ambiguity from how compound expressions are parsed and understood.
history: Languages define precedence and associativity conventions to reduce parentheses while retaining a deterministic parse.
mental_model: Build a grouping tree first; then evaluate operands and operators under language-defined rules.
analogy: Parentheses in arithmetic group work; the analogy fails because programming includes assignment, coercion, short-circuiting, and effects.
common_mistakes: Adding parentheses that preserve parser behavior but not reader clarity
industry_notes: Explicit grouping is justified when it communicates intent or protects maintenance, not merely when syntax requires it.
ai_notes: Ask AI to show the implicit grouping and a clearer equivalent before accepting a rewrite.
interview_notes: Ask the candidate to distinguish precedence, associativity, and operand evaluation order.
exercise_candidates: Insert grouping and justify whether results change
lab_candidates: Compare implicit and explicit expression trees
